full_judgment: 3. In their plaint, the plaintiffs disclosed their case stating inter alia that the Ka schedule property disclosed in the plaint originally belonged to Nezabot Ali Khan, Abdul Hakim and others and while they had been in possession of this land it was recorded in their favour during C.S. operation appertaining to khatian No.174 and Plot No.67 within Mouza Dhanmondi; Mirza Abdul Kadir one of the co-sharer of the Jamaindari Estate settled five bigas of land in favour of Sree Aboni Mohon Dey and Aboni Mohon executed a registered kabuliyat on 18-12-1940 and in course of such settlement Aboni Mohon being in possession of the said five bigas of land settled three bighas out of the same in favour of one Abdul Barek by a registered Addi Barga kabuliyat, subsequently, Aboni Mohon entered into an agreement for sale of one acres of land from the south western part of C.S. Plot No.67 with one Abdul Mazid Howlader and Begum Ayesha Noor on 29.07.47 at a consideration of Tk.3000/00 out of the said amount of Tlc.3000/00 the purchasers paid Tk.750/00 as earnest money whereupon possession was delivered in favour of the purchasers but due to partition of the country, the executant left for India so they subsequently arranged to execute and register a sale deed through an appointed attorney; meanwhile process of acquisition by the government was started through L.A. Case No.6 of 1948-49 in respect of part of Plot No.67; then one Sufia Khatun filed Writ Petition No.145 of 1965 challenging the notice issued in said L.A. Case and Rule was issued initially but subsequently the same was discharged on 19.08.1966 thereafter Sufia Khatun preferred an appeal to the Supreme Court of Pakistan being Appeal No.63-D of 1966 whereupon Pakistan Supreme Court vide its judgment and order dated 01.12.1967 allowed the appeal declaring the notice of acquisition as a defective one; it is also disclosed in the plaint that husband of Begum Aysha Nur was assured by the then C&B by its letter No.104 TP dated 15.01.53 for making construction on the suit property upon receipt of Government plan; thereafter, it is also stated in the plaint, that Ka schedule property along with some other properties were relieved from the acquisition process; on 26-10-56 one Ashutosh Dey Sarker being appointed as attorney of Aboni Mohon Dey executed and registered a sale deed in favour of Abdul Mojid Howlader and Ayesha Nur, thereafter Abdul Mojid Howlader transferred a area of 8 khatas of land from the suit plot in favour of one M. A. Goni and Afaiuddin Khan by a kabala dated 31.07.57 subsequently Mojid Howlader transferred the remaining 22 khatas of land by oral gift to predecessor of the 'plaintiffs Begum Ayesha Noor and since then Ayesha Noor had been possessing the schedule property till 03-10-2000 on which date she died leaving behind the plaintiffs as her legal heirs; the plaintiffs and their predecessors had been in possession of the suit property by constructing 16 shop rooms inducting tenants for more than 48 years and those shop rooms were rented in favour of different persons as tenants who had been running their business concerns in those rooms; while the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land as aforesaid RAJUK in collusion with the defendants demolished the structures constructed by the plaintiffs over the suit land and in the process RAJUK obtained an Aungikemama (bond) from the plaintiff No.1 under pressure; thereafter RAJUK again demolished the structures of the plaintiffs over the suit land by bulldozer in collusion with the husband of defendant No.6 with the aid of hired miscreants; after demolishing plaintiffs structures in the suit land on 30-03-2001 defendants dis-possessed the plaintiffs from the Ka schedule property by installing fencing with tin around it; they also constructed some rooms in the site; it is also stated in the plaint that the police did not take action against the influential invaders; lastly on 20.04.2001 a G.D. Entry could be made by the plaintiffs over the act of their dispossession on 30.03.2001. It is also stated in the plaint that the defendants are strangers who have dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land using RAJUK as a tool for their mischief.
